policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the conjunction and negation as ‘and hath not pitied,’ distinguishing qere וְלֹא from ketiv לא.
ASV’s ‘to bring back thy captivity’ renders qere שְׁבוּתֵךְ; the alternative-rendering note concerns English wording and does not support the ketiv.
ASV’s absolute phrase ‘in the night,’ followed separately by ‘at the beginning of the watches,’ distinguishes qere בַלַּיְלָה from ketiv construct בליל.
